key_insight: Laya-IsoToken enables clinical codebook switching without target-labeled training notes by separating clinical evidence extraction from code definitions.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce reannotation burdens when hospitals update coding systems, reimbursement groupers, or coding languages.
method: Train a clinical span reader once against a frozen multilingual concept space, with no per-code classifier parameters.
Compile public target code descriptions into alignment operators in under three seconds.
Route unfamiliar concepts to offline language-model verification using a geometric residual.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 62.6% Micro-F1 on 32,804 ICD-9 discharges, switching to 13,783 unseen-patient ICD-10 discharges without target training notes, and 40.6% ICD-10 Micro-F1 with offline verification on 1,000 summaries.
watch_item: Reported benchmark performance does not establish deployment readiness; prospective validation across hospitals and assessment of verifier costs remain important.
paper_title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
